lines: Persistent breathing difficulties
He was born prematurely at 27 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery after a complicated pregnancy and was admitted to the NICU shortly after birth.
The mother recalls he required prolonged respiratory support and oxygen for several weeks and was discharged on home oxygen therapy.
Since then, he has had frequent outpatient visits for wheezing and mild respiratory distress but no hospital readmissions.
The parents say he tires easily during feeding and has not reached the same weight as other children his age.

- Metastatic neuroblastoma with bone involvement
- History of treated congenital syphilis

- Developmental delay
- Patent ductus arteriosus ligation
- Resection of adrenal neuroblastoma
- Placement of tunneled central venous catheter
- Bone marrow biopsy

- Cyclophosphamide (maintenance chemotherapy) As per oncology protocol
No known drug allergies
